transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… it’s a little embarrassing. At church I’ve been doing odd things. Like I’ll stand by the potluck table holding the serving spoon up and just… not move. Or I’ll keep folding the same napkins over and over while folks are waiting. I don’t know why.

When you're standing there holding the spoon or repeating the folding, do you feel like you're stuck and can't make your body move even though you want to, or does it feel more like you have an urge you have to keep acting on?

I don’t know that it feels like either one exactly. I just… find myself doing it. Standing there with the spoon up, or folding the same napkins again and again, and people are waiting. It’s odd, I know.
Have you had behaviors like this—getting stuck in a position or repeating an action—since childhood, or is this something new that started recently?
No… not since I was little. This is newer. I guess people started noticing it maybe… six months ago or so. The odd things, and sometimes me not making much sense when I talk.

In the past six months, have you noticed periods where your mood felt unusually high, euphoric, or irritable, along with needing much less sleep than usual or feeling like you had way more energy or big plans than normal?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t felt, you know, especially high or full of energy like that. Sleep’s just… I don’t know, but not like that.
Over the past six months, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or like you’ve lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve been sad all the time. Things don’t feel quite the same, maybe, but I can’t really say I’ve lost interest like that.
Have you experienced hearing voices or seeing things that others don't, or had strong beliefs that others find unusual or that others say aren't true?
I’m… not sure. I don’t think I’ve seen anything like that. Voices… I don’t really know. People say I get mixed up about things sometimes, but I don’t want to say more than that.
Have you had any recent medical problems, head injury, seizures, infections, or started any new medications or substances around the time these behaviors began?
I don’t think so… nothing that I remember like that. I haven’t had, um, some big injury or anything. I’m not sure about all the rest.
Have you noticed your confusion or 'getting mixed up' come and go throughout the day—like clearer at some moments and more muddled at others—or has it stayed pretty much the same the whole time?
I’m not really sure. I don’t keep track of it like that… some times I feel a little clearer, maybe, but I can’t say if it changes through the day.
In the past six months, have you noticed any fevers, unexplained weight loss, tremors, or times when your heart was racing or you were sweating a lot for no clear reason?
I haven’t really noticed anything like that… no. I mean, I don’t keep close track, but nothing comes to mind.

Besides these episodes of freezing or repeating actions, have you noticed changes in how you show emotion—like your face seeming less expressive, or your voice sounding flatter than before—or have you been pulling away from people and activities you used to be part of?

I guess I’ve pulled back some. I used to help more with choir and church things, but… I mix up plans sometimes, or people, and then folks get uncomfortable or someone has to fix what I did. So I just don’t do as much now.

When people say you're not making sense or getting mixed up while talking, can you tell me more about that—do you notice your thoughts jumping between unrelated topics, or is it more that you forget words or lose track of what you were saying?

I guess it’s more my thoughts run off. Like… the ladies ask me something simple, about blankets or choir practice, and I mean to answer right. But then I’m talking about beans, or a hymn, or my roses, and they look at me like they can’t follow it.

When someone gently tries to move your arm or reposition you during one of these episodes, do you notice yourself resisting the movement, or does your arm stay in the new position they placed it in, almost like it's waxy or moldable?

I… I don’t know about the arm part so much. What I notice is at church I do odd things, like I’ll stand by the potluck table holding the serving spoon up and just not move, or I’ll fold the same napkins over and over while folks are waiting.
During these episodes when you're frozen or repeating an action, do you also stop talking altogether, even when someone speaks directly to you?
I’m not really sure. I don’t notice that part much. Folks may talk to me and I’m just… busy with the thing, I guess. I don’t know if I stop talking altogether.
When someone at church asks you to stop what you're doing or to move, do you find yourself doing the opposite of what they ask, or refusing to respond at all?

I don’t know if I’m trying to do the opposite. I just… get stuck doing odd things, like standing there by the potluck with the serving spoon up, or folding the napkins again and again while people are waiting.
Do you ever notice yourself laughing, smiling, or reacting emotionally in a way that doesn't seem to match what's actually happening around you?

I don’t know about laughing or smiling wrong. I just know I came because at church I keep doing odd things… like standing there by the potluck table with the serving spoon up, not moving, or folding the same napkins over and over while people are waiting.
Do you ever notice yourself repeating back the exact words someone just said to you, or copying their movements or gestures without meaning to?

I don’t know about repeating words or copying folks. What I know is I keep doing odd things at church… standing there with the serving spoon held up, or folding the same napkins over and over while people are waiting.
Does the mixed-up, rambling speech happen mainly during those times when you're frozen or repeating an action, or do you notice it happening at other times too, even when you're not stuck like that?

It happens other times too, I think. Like if the ladies ask me about blankets or choir practice, I mean to answer right, but then my words… they go off. I’ll be talking about beans, then hymns, then my roses, and people just look at me confused.

I’m not real sure how long. It feels like I just… get stuck there. At church, by the potluck table, holding the serving spoon up, or with those same napkins in my hands folding them again and again while folks are waiting.
Have the people at church told you how long you stay stuck like that—do they say it's just a moment, or more like several minutes or longer?

They don’t really tell me a time. They just say I’m standing there too long… with the spoon up, or messing with the same napkins while folks are waiting. I don’t know if it’s minutes. It feels all mixed up.
How often would you say these 'stuck' episodes with the spoon or napkins happen—every day, a few times a week, or only once in a while?

Only once in a while, I think… enough that folks at church notice. I came in because I keep doing odd things there, like standing with the serving spoon up, or folding the same napkins again and again while people are waiting.
